H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper defines four sequential stages only: GPS following, vision position following, ground-effect free trajectory following, and shutdown; no parent/child or composite state structure is described.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions depend on relative UAV-platform geometry: a 0.1 m spherical domain centered 1.1 m behind and 0.7 m above the pad, plus visibility/estimation loss, trajectory divergence, altitude, overshoot, and landing thresholds.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: States issue continuous control actions: GPS following offsets, PID-generated velocity setpoints, optimized trajectory following, rapid safe separation on rollback, and motor throttle shutdown.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: Vision loss rolls the controller back to GPS guidance, and Stage 3 failsafe conditions roll back to vision following while separating the UAV from the platform.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names are listed in the FSM section, Stage 3 behavior is expanded in the trajectory-planner section, and concrete failsafe thresholds/examples appear later in outdoor experiments.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as convergence reading, failsafe, safe distance, and ground-effect free trajectory require UAV-domain interpretation beyond a literal state list.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are embedded in narrative stage descriptions rather than a state/action table: velocity-command generation, trajectory generation, safe separation, and throttle reduction.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: At least one guard is a 3D relative-position sphere; other guards combine altitude, horizontal offset, overshoot, trajectory divergence, and estimator availability.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite parent state with its own entry/during/exit behavior is present.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Recovery transitions are local to vision loss and Stage 3 failsafe rollback, not declared as an any-state global escape.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The sample has several numeric and boolean guards over relative pose, estimator availability, altitude, overshoot, and landing thresholds.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The rollback rules are local to specific stages and do not create an N-to-1 cross-cutting transition advantage over multiple substates.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Some actions are high-level controller effects such as safe separation and trajectory generation, but many are concrete flight-controller or motor commands.

one_line_pitch: A flat but guard-heavy UAV landing supervisor whose spatial handoff, failsafe rollback, and shutdown actions stress guard and action extraction much more than simple event-driven FSMs.
rationale: The actual paper supports the STM extraction: it is a four-stage landing supervisor with meaningful spatial guards, per-stage control actions, and dedicated rollback behavior. It is not a hierarchy stress case, but it strongly targets guard and action weaknesses in Umple-style baselines. Baseline difficulty is high because state behavior is distributed across the FSM, trajectory-planning, and experiment sections, with several domain terms and implicit action attributions.
